short: Seventy years on the throne, from empire and rationing to the internet age.
full:
Elizabeth II was in Kenya when her father died in February 1952. Her coronation the following June was the first to be televised, watched by an estimated twenty million people in Britain, and it set the pattern for a reign conducted in public.

She worked with fifteen prime ministers from Churchill onwards and held weekly audiences with all of them, keeping her own opinions unpublished throughout. Most of the remaining colonies became independent during her reign, many of them joining a Commonwealth she treated as a personal commitment, and she remained head of state of more than a dozen other realms. The institution took damage in the 1990s from her children's divorces, the Windsor Castle fire and the public reaction to the death of Diana, Princess of Wales, in 1997, and recovered through the golden and diamond jubilees. She died at Balmoral on 8 September 2022, aged 96, the longest-reigning British monarch.
